column1: # mapping_set_title: "NTIA SBOM Minimum Elements <-> SEMIC vocabularies"

# mapping_set_description: "Maps the 7 minimum-element concepts defined in 'The Minimum Elements For a Software Bill of Materials' (NTIA, November 2021) to DCAT-AP, Schema.org, and related SEMIC vocabularies widely used for cataloguing datasets and software. The sbom: bridge concept in see_also is the shared abstraction that also connects NTIA to SPDX 3.1 and other target formats."

column8: The agent(s) that produced the SBOM document; dcterms:creator is "an entity primarily responsible for making the resource" — close semantic match
schema:author on a schema:DigitalDocument corresponds directly to the SBOM author
dcterms:created is "date of creation of the resource"; SBOM timestamp is when the SBOM was made — close match; dcterms:issued (formal publication) is less precise here
schema:dateCreated is the date of creation of the item — exact semantic match for SBOM creation timestamp
schema:name on a schema:SoftwareApplication or schema:Product provides the human-readable component name
dcterms:title is commonly used for the name of a catalogued resource; relatedMatch because title implies a formal heading rather than a product name
schema:softwareVersion on schema:SoftwareApplication carries the version string
dcat:version is "the version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource"; relatedMatch because it applies to datasets/distributions rather than software specifically
dcterms:publisher is "an entity responsible for making the resource available" — overlaps with distributor role of supplier but misses the manufacturer role

schema:manufacturer is the organization that produced the component — better match for the original-vendor aspect of supplier; neither dcterms:publisher nor schema:manufacturer alone covers both roles
dcterms:identifier is "an unambiguous reference to the resource"; covers PURL, CPE, SWID and other stable IDs
schema:identifier is a structured identifier property applicable to any schema:Thing including software packages

dcterms:hasPart ("a related resource that is included physically or logically in the described resource") approximates the CONTAINS relationship; dependency relationships in general require a typed predicate (CONTAINS, DEPENDS_ON, etc.) that dcterms does not provide
schema:hasPart similarly approximates part-of/component relationships; same limitation as dcterms:hasPart regarding typed dependency semantics
